sources.entry: zest - Autocomplete popup for zsh with descriptions for 1,500 commands, in Terminal.app, iTerm2, Ghostty, VS Code and Cursor. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/rostik32/zest) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: zest is a native Swift autocomplete popup for zsh on macOS that shows subcommands, options, files and git branches with descriptions under the cursor in Terminal, iTerm2, Ghostty, VS Code and Cursor.
summary.what_it_does: zest shows an autocomplete popup while you type a command in zsh, offering subcommands, options, files, folders, git branches and command history, each with a description. It ships with specs for about 1,500 commands, drawn from the open-source Fig spec collection, plus AI coding agent commands. New specs are plain YAML files, and `zest gen` can draft one from a command's --help output. The popup can use 74 VS Code themes, or follow the current VS Code or Cursor theme, with optional descriptions and configurable rows, font and width. The README says the app runs locally and makes network requests only to check GitHub for updates, which can be disabled. Tab, arrow keys, Enter and Esc control the popup, and the shell sends each keystroke to the app without waiting.
use_cases: get command suggestions with descriptions while typing in zsh on a Mac
add autocomplete for a custom CLI tool via a YAML spec
replace Fig or Amazon Q CLI autocomplete with a local app
complete git branch names and file paths in the terminal
style the terminal completion popup to match a VS Code theme
draft a command spec from its --help output
how_to_run: xcode-select --install && git clone <repo> && cd zest && make install
notable: Native Swift menu bar app with no Electron or web view; the README reports about 20-30 MB memory and a ~3 MB binary
Ships about 1,500 command specs from the Fig spec collection, plus AI coding agent commands
Draft a new spec from a command's --help with `zest gen`
74 themes converted from VS Code, or the current VS Code/Cursor theme
Shell sends keystrokes asynchronously over a local Unix socket, with measured sub-millisecond per-key cost
caveats: Requires macOS 14 or later on Apple silicon; Intel Macs are not supported
Only zsh is supported; bash and fish are not yet supported
The app is not signed or notarized by Apple, so manual install needs a Privacy & Security override (the install script and Homebrew cask avoid this)
